claims.text: Structural and chemical stability is governed by competition between configurational entropy and strain energy from atomic-size and bonding differences.
At lower temperatures, configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered solid solution.
Increasing temperature enhances atomic mobility and permits strain energy to drive atomic clustering and ordering.
Thermally induced clustering and ordering degrade the initially homogeneous phase.
The initial nanoparticles contain five or more metals in near-equal atomic ratios and are disordered solid solutions.
Al0.1CrCoFeNi is an example of an equimolar or near-equimolar five-component HEA.
The controlled thermal comparison spans approximately 473 K to 1923 K.
Using an inert or controlled atmosphere and no external mechanical stress minimizes oxidation and mechanically induced rearrangement.
Atomic-size and bonding differences produce local strain fields that drive short-range ordering or atomic clustering.
Clustering lowers free energy by relieving local strain energy.
Nanoparticles held near 473 K will largely retain their disordered solid-solution structure.
Exposure at temperatures approaching 1923 K will produce a measurable increase in atomic clustering and ordering relative to the low-temperature baseline.
High-temperature ordering will be accompanied by changes in lattice parameters.
High-temperature structural changes will correspond to variations in catalytic or thermoelectric performance.
The initial or 473 K baseline has negligible short-range order.
Oxidation and mechanical stress can alter atomic mobility or the relevant energy balance.
The temperature at which ordering becomes significant varies with alloy composition and operating conditions.
Ordering kinetics may produce either gradual or abrupt structural changes.
XRD, HRTEM, and APT can be used to measure phase evolution, lattice shifts, ordering, and nanoscale compositional clustering.
Failure to observe increased clustering or ordering through 1923 K, or failure to observe the predicted structure-performance correlation, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Al0.1CrCoFeNi is repeatedly described as equimolar or near-equimolar, but normalizing the stated stoichiometry gives approximately 2.44 at.% Al and 24.39 at.% each of Cr, Co, Fe, and Ni, which is not near-equal.
